targetdiff_inputs.title: TargetDiff Input Files and Sampling Configuration
targetdiff_inputs.content:
<data_description>TargetDiff samples 3D candidate ligand molecules conditioned on a protein binding-pocket structure. The upstream README describes sampling from a pocket PDB, typically a 10 angstrom region around a reference ligand. This service uses the included pretrained checkpoint and does not need the training dataset at inference time.</data_description>

<input_files>
[.pdb, .json]
</input_files>

<input_schema>
{
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "seed": {"type": "integer", "default": 2021},
    "num_samples": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 100, "default": 10},
    "num_steps": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 1000, "default": 100},
    "batch_size": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 32, "default": 16}
  }
}
</input_schema>

Provide exactly one pocket PDB file and at most one optional JSON file. For example, the JSON file may contain {"num_samples": 5, "num_steps": 100, "batch_size": 5}. Larger sample counts and step counts increase runtime. The returned SDF and SMILES contain generated candidates; the JSON summary reports reconstruction metrics and does not indicate binding affinity or biological activity.

targetdiff_paper.title: TargetDiff Research Paper
targetdiff_paper.content: <data_description>TargetDiff is a 3D equivariant diffusion model for target-aware molecule generation and affinity prediction, introduced at ICLR 2023. In this serving configuration, the upstream pocket-sampling workflow is exposed as molecule generation from a supplied protein pocket. This endpoint does not run the paper's affinity-prediction workflow and does not calculate binding affinity for generated molecules.</data_description>
